dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member with rights to update business rules.
Set up at least two business rules for testing update and duplicate-key scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a business rule by ID as an admin user. First create a business rule, then delete it and verify the rule is no longer retrievable through normal list or get endpoints (unless soft-deleted items are explicitly included). Attempt to delete a rule that does not exist and verify that a clear error is returned. Test repeated delete requests on the same rule and confirm proper error handling. Ensure audit logging or compliance policies are respected if defined by business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin member to authenticate as the deleter.
Create a business rule to be deleted in the test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of policy change log records as an authenticated admin. Provide filter parameters such as change type (e.g., 'EDIT'), date range (e.g., only logs from last week), actor admin ID, or affected policy/rule ID in the request body. Verify correct pagination, sorting, and filtering of results, with the total/result count and relevant fields present. Confirm that only authenticated admins can access this endpoint. Attempt retrieval as a non-admin (e.g., member) and verify access is denied with a proper error code. Edge cases: Test with invalid filter formats and verify appropriate error responses are provided.

dependencies.purpose: Creates one or more policy change logs in advance to ensure log listings return appropriate records for test filtering/pagination.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving full details for a specific policy change log by its unique ID as an authenticated admin. First, create a new policy change log and retrieve its ID. Then fetch its detail using the endpoint and verify all expected fields (actor, type, before/after, timestamp, reference) are present. Also, attempt retrieval as a non-admin and as an admin for a non-existent ID, verifying 403/404 errors as appropriate.

dependencies.purpose: Create a known policy change log to use its ID for detail retrieval and error case simulation.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a policy change log as an authenticated admin by providing all required fields with valid references to the changed policy or business rule, change type, before/after JSON, and timestamp. Upon success, verify that the log is persisted and returned with correct details. Test error cases: (1) Attempt creation with missing required fields, (2) Provide invalid references (e.g., non-existent policy/rule/actor), and (3) Attempt creation as a non-admin. Ensure appropriate errors are returned in each scenario.

dependencies.purpose: Set up an admin account for testing as the actor admin.
Optionally create a content policy to reference in the policy change log being created.
Optionally create a business rule to reference in the policy change log being created.

scenario.draft: Test an authenticated admin updating details of an existing policy change log (e.g., append or correct audit notes, update before/after values, or change reference). First, create a policy change log, then perform a valid update. Verify the updated fields are reflected correctly and audit fields updated. Edge cases: (1) Attempt update with invalid data (e.g., reference to non-existent policy/rule), (2) Attempt update as non-admin, (3) Try updating a non-existent log. Each should return appropriate error codes/data.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy change log for use in update scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a policy change log as an authenticated admin. First, create a new policy change log, then delete it and confirm the removal (or soft-delete, per business rules). Attempt deletion on a non-existent log and as a non-admin, verifying error and audit behaviors. Confirm deletion is itself logged per business rules and deleted log is absent (or properly marked) in subsequent GET calls.

dependencies.purpose: Create a policy change log for controlled deletion and negative case testing.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated list of moderation appeals as an admin, including advanced filtering such as by action ID, appeal status, and date range. First, ensure there are multiple moderation appeals in various states by creating appeals via the creation endpoint with assorted attributes. As an admin, request a list of appeals with specific pagination and filter parameters. Validate response metadata (pagination correctness) and ensure that only appeals matching the filter criteria are returned. Check for correct handling of missing or malformed filter parameters (error responses).

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple moderation appeal records in diverse states to be retrieved and filtered during the list operation. Appeals should have varied members, statuses, dates, and actions.

scenario.draft: Test that only users with moderator or admin roles can access the moderation appeals listing and that unauthorized roles (such as unauthenticated users or standard members) are denied access. Attempt to retrieve the list as a user without the required role and validate appropriate authorization or forbidden errors. Ensure compliance with security/privacy policies.

Test that requesting a list of moderation appeals with filter criteria that match no records returns an empty result set and pagination metadata indicating zero results. Use advanced search filters for non-existent criteria and verify response structure and correctness.

Test retrieving a specific moderation appeal by its unique ID as a moderator or admin. First create a moderation appeal, then fetch its details using the returned ID. Validate that all fields match the expected values from creation and that access is allowed for privileged users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation appeal record and capture its ID for retrieval testing.

scenario.draft: Test that users who are neither the owner, a moderator, nor admin cannot access the details of an appeal they do not own. Attempt to access the appeal as a standard user, confirming the correct forbidden error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation appeal to test access control restrictions by trying to fetch it as an unauthorized user.

scenario.draft: Test the system response when retrieving a moderation appeal that does not exist (invalid or deleted ID). Use a random UUID or remove an existing appeal and then attempt to fetch it, verifying a not found error is returned.

Test successful creation of a moderation appeal by a member. Prepare an eligible moderation action, then submit a valid appeal request (with rationale and references). Check that the response includes all correct fields, status is 'pending', and audit trails (timestamps) are populated.

Test failure scenarios for appeal creation due to missing required fields (such as missing rationale or invalid moderation action reference) or invalid input formats. Submit malformed request bodies and validate that validation errors are correctly returned with explanatory messages.

Test creation of a duplicate appeal (same member, same moderation action, status pending/undecided). Create an initial moderation appeal, then attempt to create another with identical keys and status. Validate that the system rejects the duplicate with a conflict error, maintaining uniqueness and business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create the first moderation appeal to establish the unique constraint, then attempt to create a duplicate for testing conflict handling.

scenario.draft: Test that a member (appeal owner) can successfully update their moderation appeal reason or withdraw a pending appeal. Create an appeal, then update the rationale or mark as withdrawn before a decision is made. Check account changes and confirm audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal as a member, to be updated prior to being decided.

scenario.draft: Test enforcement of business rules preventing updates to appeals after their status is decided/resolved. Create and process an appeal so that status is no longer pending, then attempt to update and confirm error response and unchanged record state.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal and progress it to a decided/resolved state using the decision endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test that only the original appeal owner or authorized moderator/admin can update an appeal. Attempt updates by other users and verify access is denied. Confirm error messages and that no update occurs.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal under one user, then attempt to update the same record as a different user.

scenario.draft: Test successful withdrawal (soft-delete) of a moderation appeal by the owner before it is decided. Create an appeal and verify that withdrawing it as the owning member sets the appropriate deleted or withdrawn status, with audit trails updated. Validate the response and confirm the appeal is no longer active.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal so the owner can later withdraw it while still pending.

scenario.draft: Test that once a moderation appeal is decided or resolved, withdrawal or deletion is not permitted. Create and process an appeal, then attempt to withdraw/delete it post-decision. Confirm the system's error response and unchanged record status for integrity and compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal and process it to decision, then attempt to withdraw after finalization.

scenario.draft: Test that only the appeal owner or authorized moderator/admin can withdraw/soft-delete a moderation appeal. Attempt deletion by another user and validate proper forbidden/error response. Ensure business logic and permissions are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an appeal under one member, then attempt to withdraw it as a different user (non-owner, non-privileged).

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin or moderator can retrieve a paginated list of moderation actions without supplying any filters, ensuring that the default pagination and permission controls are respected. The scenario confirms the response includes valid moderation action entries and appropriate metadata, and that unauthorized users cannot access this resource.

dependencies.purpose: Create both an admin and a moderator account to be used for authentication and verifying role-based access to moderation actions.

scenario.draft: Test the capability of an authorized moderator or admin to search moderation actions using advanced filters, such as filtering by actor (moderator/admin), target member, action type (suspend, warn, edit), and date range. This includes verifying that the filtered results correspond to the requested criteria and that malformed or unauthorized filter attempts are handled with error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple moderation actions with varying attributes (different actors, target members, types, dates) to ensure the search/filter functionality can be thoroughly verified.

scenario.draft: Check that a moderator or admin can retrieve the full details of a specific moderation action by its unique ID. The test should create a new moderation action, extract its ID, and then fetch details, verifying all information matches the original record. Also, verify the audit fields and cross-references (actor/member/content) are present.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action, returning its ID for use in the detail fetch scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that requesting a moderation action with a non-existent or malformed ID returns a proper not-found (404) error response, with no sensitive information leaked and appropriate error messaging for audit and compliance.

Ensure an admin or moderator can successfully create a moderation action by submitting valid data (including action type, actor, reason, and linkages to affected member and content). On success, the response should return all required fields, proper timestamps, and reference integrity. This scenario prepares for subsequent update, fetch, and list test coverage.

dependencies.purpose: Create moderator/admin users to act as the moderator and target member for the moderation action.

scenario.draft: Test the API's validation logic for moderation action creation by submitting incomplete or invalid data (e.g., missing required fields like action type or linkages). The system must reject the request with a descriptive error, ensuring data integrity and compliance.

Attempt to create a moderation action while authenticated as a regular member (or without authentication), and verify that access is denied with a forbidden (403) error and that no moderation action is created.

dependencies.purpose: Create a non-privileged member account to test forbidden access when attempting to create a moderation action.

scenario.draft: Validate that an admin or moderator can update a moderation action by providing a valid update payload (e.g., editing the rationale or the action notes), and that the response contains the updated record reflecting the new data. Audit trails must reflect the change.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action record as setup for the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action using invalid input (e.g., invalid field types or values, or attempts to modify immutable fields). The system must reject the request and return descriptive validation errors without altering the original record.

dependencies.purpose: Create a valid moderation action as the initial record to be used for invalid update testing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action as an unauthorized user (regular member), verifying that the system denies the update and returns a forbidden error, and that no changes are made to the moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to provide a record for access denial tests.
Create a non-privileged member to use as the unauthorized actor.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a moderator or admin can delete a moderation action record by ID, confirming that the deletion is soft (audit trail persists) and that subsequent fetches for the deleted record respond appropriately (e.g., not found or marked as deleted).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Verify that an unauthorized user (regular member or unauthenticated client) cannot delete a moderation action, and that the system returns an appropriate error and the action remains unaffected.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action for which unauthorized deletion requests can be issued.
Create a non-privileged member for use in unauthorized access test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated, filtered list of post reactions using various filters such as member, post, reaction type, and creation timestamp. Begin by creating sample members with different roles (member, moderator, admin), posts to receive reactions, and add multiple post reactions from different users. Try retrieving post reactions as an authorized user with filter criteria such as by post, by member, by reaction type, and date range. Validate pagination, sorting, and correct data exposure depending on role/authorization. Also, test requesting with invalid filters or parameters (e.g., invalid UUIDs or out-of-range values) to confirm error handling. Confirm that unauthorized users cannot access restricted reactions, and that only visible data is returned to users with proper permission levels.

dependencies.purpose: Create authenticated members with different roles for the reactions tests.
Create discussion board posts to serve as targets for post reactions.
Generate multiple post reactions with various types and linked users/posts for query diversity.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific post reaction by its unique identifier. First, create a member and a post, then add a reaction to that post. Retrieve the reaction by its ID and validate that all fields are correct and accessible to the authorized user. Next, attempt to fetch a post reaction using a non-existent or invalid ID to verify that proper error responses are returned. Finally, test retrieval by an unauthorized user to check role-based access restrictions and privacy enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Setup a valid member for creating post reactions.
Create a discussion post to serve as the target for the reaction.
Create the post reaction whose ID will be used for detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new post reaction as an authenticated user. First, set up a member and a post as the reaction target. Successfully create a post reaction with allowed values (e.g., like or dislike) and verify the created object fields. Next, attempt to create a duplicate post reaction by the same user on the same post to confirm the unique constraint enforcement and receive a conflict error. Also, test with invalid input cases such as missing fields, invalid reaction types, non-existent post or user references, and unauthorized attempts. Ensure each error is handled with a descriptive response according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will react to posts.
Create a discussion post to react to.

scenario.draft: Test updating a post reaction as the original reaction creator and as an authorized moderator. First, setup a member, a post, and a post reaction. Successfully update the reaction type (e.g., from like to dislike) and check that changes are reflected, and timestamps are updated. Attempt to update the reaction by a different non-authorized member and confirm that permission errors are returned. Also, try changing to an invalid reaction type or updating with malformed data to test validation logic. Check for correct error responses and audit trail updates (if applicable).

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for the original reaction and another user for testing unauthorized updates.
Create the post to receive the reaction.
Create the original post reaction to later update.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a post reaction (soft delete) as both the original creator and as a moderator. First, create a member, a post, and a post reaction. Delete the reaction as the creator and verify that the reaction is marked deleted, but the record remains for audit. Also, attempt deletion as a moderator to ensure administrative delete capability. Then, try deleting as an unauthorized user and verify that access is denied. Attempt to delete a non-existent or already-deleted reaction to confirm proper error responses and idempotence. Confirm that deleted reactions do not appear in standard queries but can be recovered in audit or admin views if permitted.

dependencies.purpose: Set up both a reacting user and a moderator (if separate roles exist).
Create the post to which the reaction was attached.
Create the post reaction to be deleted in various scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of configuration settings with various filtering and pagination options. Confirm that the configuration list can be filtered by key, value, or description with both partial and full matches, and that pagination metadata and constraints are respected (e.g., page size, out-of-bounds requests). Ensure only non-deleted configurations appear unless system role settings request otherwise. Include scenarios accounting for malformed filter parameters, ensuring error responses are returned as specified. Confirm audit filtering and permission boundaries for sensitive settings.

Test failure response when attempting to list configuration settings using invalid or malformed filter criteria or pagination parameters (e.g., non-numeric page, invalid date format, unknown sort field). System should return validation error with appropriate code/message and avoid exposing sensitive or unintended configuration data.

Verify that when using admin or system-level search, the list endpoint can include soft-deleted (archived) configurations if explicitly requested, and that sensitive fields or settings are visible only if caller has appropriate permissions. Contrast with regular user/member query which should exclude such records.

dependencies.purpose: Create standard member and admin users for verifying permission boundaries when retrieving configurations including soft-deleted records.
Create sample configuration parameters, both active and soft-deleted, to ensure realistic test of results returned by list endpoint under different roles and filters.

scenario.draft: Test the configuration list endpoint when no configurations are present, or when paginating beyond the last page. The endpoint should return an empty result set, valid pagination metadata, and no errors in the normal case; ensure proper system stability with zero or sparse data.

Test successful retrieval of configuration details by valid ID. Create a configuration entry as an admin, then retrieve it as both the creator (admin) and a member with sufficient permissions. Confirm the configuration's detailed attributes (key, value, description, timestamps) are returned as expected and permission rules are correctly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one admin and regular member to test varied permission scenarios for configuration retrieval.
Create a new configuration record to serve as the target for detail retrieval by ID.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a configuration by an ID that does not exist in the system. Expect a not-found error with appropriate code and message, and ensure no sensitive data is revealed. Try with both admin and member access for this error path.

Test the access restrictions and response when retrieving a configuration entry that has been soft-deleted. Scenario should verify that an admin or privileged user can access and view details of the soft-deleted entry, while a member without sufficient privileges cannot retrieve or should receive a not-found or forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin and regular user accounts to validate permission checks for soft-deleted configuration visibility.
Create a configuration entry; will be soft-deleted for the scenario.
Soft-delete the configuration so its retrieval can be tested across roles.

scenario.draft: Test the successful creation of a new configuration entry using valid inputs (unique key, proper value, optional description). Ensure the response includes all metadata and that the configuration appears in system-wide listings. Confirm audit log or creation timestamp is set as required by business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user authorized to perform configuration creation.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a configuration with a key that already exists, expecting a uniqueness violation and proper error response. First, create a configuration as an admin, then attempt to create another using the same key.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for setup.
Create the initial configuration to set up the uniqueness conflict.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a configuration without required fields (such as missing key) or with inputs violating schema constraints. Ensure that the system returns validation errors with clear messages about the invalid or missing properties and does not create any configuration entry.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user authorized to perform creation attempts with invalid data.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a configuration record while authenticated as a regular member or other role lacking 'admin' privileges. The attempt should be denied with permission error, and no configuration record should be created. Confirm that proper error code and message are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create both admin and member users to verify permission boundaries for the configuration creation endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an existing configuration's value and optional description fields by an authorized admin. Create a configuration entry, update relevant fields, and confirm in the response that changes are persisted (and reflected on subsequent GET/patch). Audit log or update timestamp should be set appropriately.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for all update operations and validation.
Create configuration to be updated during the scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a configuration entry by providing invalid field values (illegal type, excessive length, prohibited values) or omitting required fields. Ensure endpoint returns appropriate validation error responses and does not apply changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin user to attempt invalid configuration update.
Create configuration to be updated.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a configuration record as a member or any role that is not an admin. Expect a permission denied error and no changes to the configuration record. Confirm error code and message meet system requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Create both admin and regular member users to test permission handling.
Create configuration record for permission denied update test.

scenario.draft: Test for uniqueness constraint when attempting to update a configuration's key to one that already exists. This should result in a conflict error rather than successful update.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for role-based access check.
Create two configuration entries; the update will try to set the second configuration's key to the first's key.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion of a configuration by an admin, ensuring that a deleted_at timestamp is set and configuration is no longer included in normal listings. Confirm that the deletion event is properly audit logged, and that the record can still be seen when querying with admin privileges including deleted entities.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user authorized for configuration deletions.
Create a configuration to serve as the deletion target.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a configuration record using an ID that does not exist. Expect a not-found error message and confirm that no change occurs in the system. Both successful and unsuccessful deletion attempts should be audit logged for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to attempt deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a configuration entry as a member or other unauthorized role. Endpoint should return a permission error and the configuration must remain undeleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create both admin and regular member users to test for permission handling on configuration deletion.
Create a configuration to serve as the deletion target.

scenario.draft: Test searching and paginating comment reaction records with various filters and sorting. Prepare multiple comments and members, and ensure at least one reaction for each combination of member, comment, and reaction type. Retrieve reactions filtered by comment ID, member ID, reaction type, and date ranges, and verify that the returned results match the expected combinations. Also, test pagination by specifying limits and offsets. Confirm that only accessible reactions are returned and soft-deleted entries are excluded from standard queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create member accounts who will participate in commenting and react to comments.
Create comment records to serve as targets for reactions.
Generate comment reaction records for use in filtering and searching scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a specific comment reaction by ID. First, create a member, a comment, and then a reaction record for that comment by the member. Fetch the reaction using the known reaction ID and verify that all fields match the initial creation. Ensure response is accurate and accessible to the authorized user or moderator.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be the reaction author.
Create a comment to attach the reaction.
Create a comment reaction whose ID will be retrieved in the test.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a comment reaction by a non-existent or improperly formatted ID. Attempt to fetch a reaction using a random UUID or non-UUID string and assert that an appropriate error (such as 404 or validation error) is returned.

Test successful creation of a comment reaction when all data is valid and the member has not yet reacted to the target comment. Ensure the returned record reflects the correct member, comment, and reaction type.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account that will react to the comment.
Create a comment to which the reaction will be attached.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a duplicate comment reaction for the same member and comment is prevented. First, create a valid reaction, then attempt to create a second reaction of the same type by the same member to the same comment. Confirm that the API returns a duplicate/conflict error as per schema constraints.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for the reaction author.
Create a comment for the reaction target.
Create the initial comment reaction to set up the duplicate constraint.

scenario.draft: Test prohibition of reaction creation using a non-existent member or comment. Attempt to submit a reaction with either an invalid member ID or comment ID and assert that the API returns the proper not found or validation error.

Test updating the reaction type of an existing comment reaction by its creator. First, a member creates a reaction, then that member updates the reaction type (e.g., from 'like' to 'dislike'). Verify the change is accepted, the correct reaction type is reflected in the result, audit timestamps are updated, and ownership requirements are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for the reaction author.
Prepare a comment target for the reaction.
Create an initial comment reaction to be updated during the test.

scenario.draft: Test that updating a comment reaction type causes a uniqueness conflict if it would duplicate an existing reaction for the same member and comment. Set up two different reactions by the same member to different comments, then attempt to update one to match the other's parameters, triggering a conflict error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to author several reactions.
Create at least two comments for reaction targets.
Create two separate reactions to set up the conflict condition for the update.

scenario.draft: Test that it is not possible for a user who is not the reaction creator or moderator to update the reaction. Set up a reaction by one member, attempt to update it as a different member, and ensure a permission/authorization error is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members to represent the owner and unauthorized party.
Create a comment for the reaction target.
Create a reaction owned by the first member, which the second member will attempt to update.

scenario.draft: Test soft-deletion of a comment reaction by its creator. After creating a member, comment, and reaction, the member deletes the reaction. Verify the record is marked deleted (not permanently removed), and a subsequent query does not return it in standard listings.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to be the owner of the reaction.
Prepare a comment to be reacted to.
Create the reaction that will be deleted.

scenario.draft: Test that a member who is not the creator, nor a moderator/admin, cannot delete a comment reaction. First, create a comment and a reaction by one user. Then attempt the delete operation as a different user, and expect an authorization/permission error in response.

dependencies.purpose: Create two members: one as the reaction owner and another as the unauthorized user.
Create a comment for the reaction target.
Create a reaction owned by the first member to be targeted for unauthorized deletion.

scenario.draft: Test deleting a comment reaction using a non-existent or invalid ID. Attempt the delete operation with an arbitrary UUID and a badly formatted string to verify that the API returns a 404 not found or validation error as required.

Test that a logged-in member can successfully retrieve their notification preferences with a filter to only include entries for 'email' notification type. The scenario involves creating a member, logging in, and subsequently creating multiple notification preferences for various types (email, push, system announcement). Then the test queries the /notificationPreferences endpoint with filtering parameters set to only email. The response should include only the relevant entries. It verifies correct filtering and access control for member users.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to act as the owner of the notification preferences.
Create multiple notification preferences (at least one with type 'email' and others with types like 'push') for the test member.

scenario.draft: Test that an administrator can retrieve a paginated and sorted list of all notification preferences in the system. This scenario verifies that, with elevated access, an admin can see preferences for any user and can sort the results (e.g., by updated timestamp descending). The test involves creating at least two members, each with different notification preferences, and then retrieving the list as an admin with pagination and sorting requests. The response should respect pagination and sorting options, returning the expected slice of results.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple member accounts for which notification preferences will be created.
Assign an admin role to a member who will perform the list operation.
Create notification preference records for each member.

scenario.draft: Test that a user can fetch their own notification preference by its unique ID. This involves creating a member, logging in, creating a notification preference for that member, and then retrieving it by ID. The scenario checks that all relevant fields are returned, and only authorized members can get their own preference. It also verifies error handling for non-existent or deleted records.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to test ownership and retrieval.
Create a notification preference for the new member.

scenario.draft: Test that a user cannot access another user's notification preference by ID. The test creates two members, a notification preference for one, and verifies that the other cannot access it, expecting a forbidden error or similar. This ensures privacy and access controls are correctly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts for access control testing.
Create a notification preference for the first member.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a notification preference for an authenticated member. Steps include creating a member, logging in, then submitting a valid creation request for a preference (e.g., enable email notifications for that user). Expectation: The preference is created, returned with correct member association and type.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to associate the preference.

scenario.draft: Test that creating a notification preference fails if the same member already has a preference of the same type (e.g., email). This checks enforcement of unique per-type preferences per member. Steps: create a member, create a preference of type 'email', then attempt to create a second 'email' preference for the same user. Expect a uniqueness or conflict error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for duplicate check.
Create a notification preference of a specific type for that member before attempting duplicate creation.

scenario.draft: Test that a user can update their own notification preference (for example, changing status from enabled to disabled or switching channels). Steps: create a member, login, create a notification preference, then update the preference. The response should return the updated details, reflecting the new configuration. Only the owner or admin should be able to update.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account as the preference owner.
Create the original notification preference to be updated.

scenario.draft: Test that another user (not the owner, nor admin) is forbidden from updating a notification preference. Steps: two members are created, a notification preference is set up for one, and then the second tries to update it. The system should reject the request with a forbidden error.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two member accounts for the forbidden scenario.
Create the notification preference for the first member.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can delete their own notification preference. Steps involve creating a member, logging in, creating a notification preference, and then deleting it by ID. The deleted preference should be marked as deleted or not retrievable in future queries.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member as the notification preference owner.
Create the notification preference record to later delete.

scenario.draft: Test the system prevents other members from deleting notification preferences they do not own. Create two members and a notification preference for the first; have the second attempt to delete it. The action should be blocked and an appropriate error returned.

dependencies.purpose: Set up multiple members including a non-owner.
Create a notification preference for the first member only.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a paginated and filtered list of content policies. Set up several content policy records with varying activation status, effective time windows, and text in the code/title/description. Check that search by code substring, activation status, and date range works. Validate that pagination, limit, offset, and sorting operate as expected. Ensure only authorized users see restricted policies if relevant. Results must align with search parameters and grant correct business policy discovery for admins and regular users.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple content policy records with various attribute combinations to test search and pagination.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of a single content policy record by its unique ID. Ensure that the returned object contains all expected fields (code, title, description, effective/expiration times, activation flags) matching the created record. Confirm correct behavior for both active and inactive (archived) policies.

dependencies.purpose: Create a dedicated content policy to fetch by ID for validation.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval failure when requesting a content policy by a non-existent or deleted ID. Verify that the system returns a clear not-found error and does not leak metadata. This ensures compliance with auditability and confidentiality requirements.

Test creating a new content policy record with all valid fields. Ensure that unique code, properly formatted title, detailed description, and correct effective/expiration timestamps are accepted. On successful creation, verify that the new record is retrievable and data matches input. Business rules for unique code and schema validation must be enforced.

Test failure when attempting to create a content policy with a duplicate code value that violates the unique constraint. First create a policy, then attempt to create another with the same code and verify the system returns a uniqueness error according to business rules. Ensure database integrity and error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Set up the first content policy with a specific code to test uniqueness violation on second attempt.

scenario.draft: Test failure when creating a content policy with an invalid effective/expiration time range (e.g., expiration before effective date). Verify the API rejects these records with a descriptive validation error, ensuring business logic and compliance for effective policy ranges.
